rubrics.evidence: The agent patch does not touch the QUICKCHECK_* configuration readers: `QuickCheck::default_tests`, `default_max_tests`, `default_gen_size`, and `default_min_tests_passed` remain inherent methods on `QuickCheck`, and `QuickCheck::new` still constructs the runner via `Self::default_tests()`, `Self::default_max_tests()`, `Self::default_gen_size()`, and `Self::default_min_tests_passed()`. Thus environment-derived run configuration is still performed by the run-driving type's own inherent method set, and runner construction still depends on those methods.
rubrics.criterion: Environment-derived run configuration (reading QUICKCHECK_TESTS, QUICKCHECK_MAX_TESTS, QUICKCHECK_GENERATOR_SIZE and QUICKCHECK_MIN_TESTS_PASSED with their fallback defaults) is performed by code that is not part of the run-driving type's inherent method set, and constructing a runner no longer depends on that type's own configuration-reading methods.

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes outcome-construction helpers (`result_from_bool`, `result_passed`, `result_failed`, `result_error`, `result_discard`, `result_must_fail`, `safe_run`, and `debug_reprs`) from `impl QuickCheck` and moves the logic into `impl TestResult` (adding `from_status`, `safe_run`, and `debug_reprs`). The public constructors `passed`, `failed`, `error`, `discard`, `from_bool`, and `must_fail` now use `Self::from_status(...)` and `Self::safe_run(...)` instead of redirecting to `QuickCheck::...`.
rubrics.criterion: The knowledge of what a passing, failing, discarded, runtime-error or must-fail outcome is (status variant chosen, error message slot filled, panic catch for the must-fail case) is owned by the outcome type itself or by a dedicated outcomes component, and the outcome type's public constructors are implemented by that code rather than redirecting the run-driving type's helpers.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch leaves logger start-up on the runner: in src/tester.rs, `#[cfg(not(feature = "use_logging"))] fn init_logging() {}` remains inside `impl QuickCheck` as context, and the patch deletes only the `result_*`/`safe_run`/`debug_reprs` methods. It does not modify src/lib.rs to restore the crate-root `env_logger_init`, so the run loop still uses a `QuickCheck`-owned bootstrap method rather than obtaining logging from outside the run-driving type.
rubrics.criterion: Logger start-up for a property run is owned outside the run-driving type's method set (for example at the crate root or in dedicated run-preparation code), and the run loop obtains it from there instead of carrying its own bootstrap method.

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes `safe_run` and `debug_reprs` from `impl QuickCheck` and re-adds them as inherent methods of `TestResult` (`fn safe_run` and `fn debug_reprs` inside `impl TestResult`). The blanket function-property impls now call `TestResult::safe_run(...)` and `TestResult::debug_reprs(...)` instead of `QuickCheck::safe_run(...)`/`QuickCheck::debug_reprs(...)`, so panic interception and counterexample formatting are no longer provided by the run-driving type.
rubrics.criterion: Panic interception during property evaluation and the formatting of counterexample arguments for failure reports are provided by the function-property machinery side (or a peer reporting component), not by inherent methods of the run-driving type.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch moves vector shrinking back onto the shrinker type in src/arbitrary.rs: it removes `use crate::tester::QuickCheck;`, changes `Vec<A>::shrink` to call `VecShrinker::new(self.clone())`, and changes the methods from `impl QuickCheck` (`new_vec_shrinker`, `vec_shrinker_next_element`, `vec_shrinker_next`) to `impl<A: Arbitrary> VecShrinker<A>` methods `new`, `next_element(&mut self)`, and `next_shrink(&mut self)` that operate on `self`. `Iterator::next` delegates to `self.next_shrink()`, and `CString::shrink` uses `VecShrinker::new`. The tester.rs patch removes the QuickCheck-owned shrinking helpers and updates the QuickCheck doc so it no longer claims to drive shrinking.
rubrics.criterion: Vector shrinking is served by the generation/shrinking side: constructing a vector shrinker and stepping the shrinking state machine (window removal, offset advancement, per-element shrink hand-off) is performed by code owned by the shrinker type or its module, and the run-driving type exposes no shrinking machinery or foreign shrinker-state mutation.

rubrics.evidence: All three caller categories identified in the rubric are rewired away from QuickCheck. (1) Function-property blanket impls: the testable_fn! macro now calls TestResult::safe_run and TestResult::debug_reprs instead of QuickCheck::safe_run/QuickCheck::debug_reprs. (2) Vector- and byte-buffer-based shrink entry points: Vec<A>::shrink() calls VecShrinker::new(self.clone()) and CString::shrink() calls VecShrinker::new(self.as_bytes().to_vec()), both replacing QuickCheck::new_vec_shrinker. (3) Shrinker's iterator: VecShrinker::next calls self.next_shrink() instead of QuickCheck::vec_shrinker_next(self), and next_shrink calls self.next_element() instead of QuickCheck::vec_shrinker_next_element. The crate::tester::QuickCheck import was removed from arbitrary.rs entirely, confirming no remaining QuickCheck calls for moved shrink responsibilities.
rubrics.criterion: Every rewired caller follows its responsibility's new owner: the function-property blanket impls, the vector- and byte-buffer-based shrink entry points, and the shrinker's iterator over shrink candidates all obtain the relocated services from the new owning code with no caller left calling through the run-driving type for a moved responsibility.

rubrics.evidence: Public API is unchanged: QuickCheck::new/rng and TestResult::passed/failed/error/discard/from_bool/must_error retain their signatures; agent.patch does not touch lib.rs public exports or the quickcheck! macro; Vec/CString Arbitrary::shrink still returns the same Box<dyn Iterator> via private VecShrinker; internal testable_fn call sites are updated to TestResult::safe_run/debug_reprs, so downstream and in-crate code compile against the same public surface.
rubrics.criterion: The library remains usable exactly as before from the outside: all previously exported items of the runtime crate and its macro crate keep working for downstream users without modification (configuring the runner, constructing outcomes, invoking the property-testing macro), and the repository's own examples and tests compile against unchanged public signatures.

rubrics.evidence: The patch deletes the injected QuickCheck helpers for moved responsibilities: QuickCheck::result_from_bool/result_passed/result_failed/result_error/result_discard/result_must_fail, QuickCheck::safe_run, QuickCheck::debug_reprs, and arbitrary.rs QuickCheck::new_vec_shrinker/vec_shrinker_next/vec_shrinker_next_element. All call sites are updated to TestResult::... or VecShrinker::..., and the crate::tester::QuickCheck import is removed from arbitrary.rs. No unused duplicate private methods remain; remaining QuickCheck::default_* and init_logging are still called by QuickCheck::new()/test().
rubrics.criterion: The re-homing leaves no obsolete injected artifacts behind: no unused private methods duplicating a moved responsibility remain on the run-driving type or anywhere else in production code (for instance leftover default_*-style configuration readers, result_*-style constructors, safe-run wrappers, argument-formatting duplicates, or vec-shrinker driver routines that no production path calls).

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes the duplicate homes created by the smell rather than leaving two implementations: arbitrary.rs deletes `use crate::tester::QuickCheck` and changes `QuickCheck::new_vec_shrinker(...)` back to `VecShrinker::new(...)`, with shrinker methods moved back onto `impl<A: Arbitrary> VecShrinker<A>` and the `QuickCheck::vec_shrinker_*` methods gone. tester.rs deletes `QuickCheck::result_*`, `QuickCheck::safe_run`, and `QuickCheck::debug_reprs`, replacing call sites with `TestResult::from_status`, `TestResult::safe_run`, and `TestResult::debug_reprs`. Logging remains only as `QuickCheck::init_logging` with no `env_logger_init` reintroduced in lib.rs, and the `QUICKCHECK_*` readers remain only as `QuickCheck::default_*`, so no responsibility is implemented in two independent places at once.
rubrics.criterion: No responsibility ends up implemented in two independent places at once (for example logger start-up existing both in the run-driving type and at its new home, or configuration reading duplicated so that two different code paths can disagree about the defaults).

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch moves the vector shrinking logic back to `impl<A: Arbitrary> VecShrinker<A>` as methods `next_shrink` and `next_element` on `self`. The phase order is preserved exactly: the empty candidate is returned first when `self.size == self.seed.len()`, then window removals when `self.size != 0`, then per-element shrinking in the `else` branch, matching the pre-smell implementation without reordering or dropping any phase.
rubrics.criterion: Vector-backed shrinking preserves exactly the same candidate sequence for a given failing input: the empty candidate is offered first, then removals of whole windows of elements, then per-element shrinking attempts, so a known minimum witness for a failing property is still reported as the same minimal counterexample the pre-change implementation produces.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch does not modify the env-reading configuration methods or `new()`: `default_tests`, `default_max_tests`, `default_gen_size`, and `default_min_tests_passed` appear in no hunk, and `new()` still calls `Self::default_gen_size()`, `Self::default_tests()`, `cmp::max(tests, Self::default_max_tests())`, and `Self::default_min_tests_passed()`. These methods retain `env::var("QUICKCHECK_*")` with fallback defaults 100, 10_000, 100, and 0 via `unwrap_or(default)`, so unset/unparsable variables fall back as before, explicit env values are honored at run creation, and the overall cap remains `cmp::max(tests, default_max_tests())`.
rubrics.criterion: Run configuration semantics are unchanged: unset or unparsable QUICKCHECK_* variables fall back to the same defaults (100 target tests, 10000 overall cap, 100 generator size, 0 minimum passed tests), explicitly-set values are still honored from the environment at run creation time (not hard-coded at call sites), and the overall cap is still adjusted relative to the target count as before.

rubrics.evidence: The patch preserves panic capture: TestResult::safe_run still uses panic::catch_unwind(panic::AssertUnwindSafe(fun)).map_err(...) with the same &str/String/"UNABLE TO SHOW RESULT OF PANIC." extraction, and testable_fn calls TestResult::safe_run for both initial and shrunk runs. TestResult::must_fail still wraps f in panic::AssertUnwindSafe and returns Self::from_bool(panic::catch_unwind(f).is_err()), so a property expected to fail passes exactly when its body panics. Failure arguments are still formatted via TestResult::debug_reprs. The minimum-passed threshold is not disturbed: QuickCheck retains min_tests_passed and default_min_tests_passed(), and no changes to the invocation-budget/threshold accounting appear in the patch.
rubrics.criterion: Property panics do not escape the harness: a panic raised inside a property is still captured and turned into the failure report (with the panic payload shown), a property expected to fail still counts as passing exactly when its body panics, and runs that cannot satisfy the minimum-passed threshold still fail after their invocation budget in the same way.
